question: Will the Kennedy Center's main building be open to the general public on October 2, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo at 2026-09-22 is CLOSED: main building fenced off since Sept 16, no public entry. The 'temporary 7-day' framing is not the binding constraint — the board voted Sept 15 to close indefinitely for repairs expected to last up to two years, echoing Trump's February 2026 announcement of a two-year renovation closure, and the NSO has already moved its whole 2026-27 season to six other DC-area venues, so no programming exists to admit a public for. Judge Cooper's rulings constrain demolition and require a sworn status report (~Sept 23) but do not order reopening; the litigation targets governance and physical changes, not operating hours. Reopening by Oct 2 would require the controlling authority to reverse itself within 11 days while physical fencing and an unrepaired Grand Foyer ceiling collapse remain. Residual YES mass is for a pretext-rebutting partial reopening (the fine print makes any few hours of access, even with theaters shut, resolve YES). No human market prices reopening; only demolition-announcement contracts exist (Polymarket 0.07-0.32, Kalshi ~0.11), which do not match this contract's subject, deadline or source, so I use them as context only.
calls.reference_class: Major venues/institutions abruptly closed to the public by their controlling authority citing safety, where that same authority is simultaneously pursuing a multi-year or permanent closure: fraction restoring public access within ~2.5 weeks
